column9: Ancient temples, UNESCO World Heritage Sites, cultural heritage (Pashupatinath, Swayambhunath, Durbar Squares)
A scenic lake city surrounded by mountains. Known for Phewa Lake, paragliding, caves, and as the starting point for Annapurna region treks. Offers both adventure and relaxation.
Diverse trek through forests, villages, and mountains
Legendary trek to the foot of Mount Everest
Short trek with stunning sunrise views
Wildlife safari park known for rhinos and jungle activities
Remote park with good chances of tiger sightings
Birthplace of Lord Buddha, spiritual monasteries
Fly like a bird over Phewa Lake and the lush Pokhara valley with panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Sarangkot is one of the world’s top paragliding destinations.
Ride thrilling rapids, enjoy calm scenic stretches, and camp riverside. Trishuli is ideal for both first-timers and experienced rafters, with grade II–III+ rapids.
Nepal’s highest trekking peak. Mera offers breathtaking views of Everest, Lhotse, and Makalu. Less technical, suitable for beginners with basic climbing experience.
A remote, challenging expedition for experienced climbers. Known for its wild terrain, fewer crowds, and beautiful trails through the Manaslu Conservation Area.

Ama Dablam is one of the most stunning peaks in the Himalayas, often called the “Matterhorn of the Himalayas.” It’s admired for its sharp, pyramid-like shape and lies on the Everest trekking route. While more technical than Everest, it attracts experienced climbers from around the world.
A center of Newari art and craftsmanship, with intricate temples, palace courtyards, and the Patan Museum. Famous for its bronze statues and wood carvings.
